title: Protocol for isolating stromal cells from lymphoid tissue for scRNA-seq
author: Makris, Shewring, et al.

In this step, collected lymph nodes will be digested, and isolated cells will be filtered. The protocol describes the optimal methods for handling the tissue and timings for digestion steps which ensure viability of stromal and immune cells. Lymph nodes are gently mixed at regular intervals and digestion mix is replaced until lymph node is fully dissociated (Figure 3A).Note: Immediately prior to starting digestion, or during initial 20 min incubation (step 5), cut 1mL pipette tips to widen the tip opening according to lymph node size (Figure 3B). This will ensure gentle passage of lymph node through the tip and increase stromal cell viability.4.Set water bath to exactly 37°C and use external thermometer to ensure temperature is appropriate (Figure 3C).CRITICAL: Ensure the temperature is precisely at 37°C. Digestion enzyme activity is greatly affected by temperature. Higher temperature causes increased digestion speed and lower temperature will decrease digestion speed. Non-optimal temperature will significantly affect stromal cell viability (see troubleshooting section – Figure 7).5.Prepare the Digestion Media and add 1.5 mL into each of the collection tubes and incubate in water bath for 20 min (Figure 3D).a.At 10 min gently tap and shake each tube and place back into water bath.CRITICAL: Prepare Digestion Media just before starting the digestion protocol and strictly maintain on ice.6.After the 20 min incubation, pipette and gently move the lymph node through the cut 1 mL pipette tip 5 times (Figure 3D).7.Once lymph nodes have settled back to the bottom of tube (Figure 3E), remove 1.5 mL of the digestion media, containing the first cell fraction and transfer to “Digested” tubes and maintain on ice.Note: Depending on the experimental objectives, “Digested” tubes can either contain FACS buffer (for flow cytometry) or MACS buffer (for MACS sorting).8.Add 1.5 mL of fresh digestion media to the samples and incubate for a further 10 min in the water bath at 37°C.9.Now switch to uncut 1 mL pipette tip and repeat steps 5–7 (Figures 3G and 3H).Note: Lymph nodes digestion time is approximately 50 min.10.Once there is no visible tissue remaining transfer all remaining digested cell suspension to the “Digested” tube and centrifuge at 350 g for 10 min at 4°C.Figure 4Composition of cells recovered after each digestion stepCollected cells were analyzed after each digestion step to determine cell phenotypes, numbers and viability. steps.title: Prepare Dispase II aliquots
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 g Dispase II in 50 mL distilled PBS, vortex on very low speed, invert a few times, then aliquot 0.5 mL into 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes and store at –80 °C for up to 12 months (final concentration 100 mg/mL).

steps.title: Prepare DNase I aliquots
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg DNase I in 10 mL distilled water, gradually mix with an additional 2.5 mL distilled water, transfer to a 15 mL Falcon tube, aliquot 0.5 mL into 1.5 mL tubes and store at –80 °C for up to 12 months (final concentration 10 mg/mL).

steps.title: Make FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 % BSA to PBS in a glass bottle, stir with a magnetic stirrer until dissolved, then add 5 mM EDTA, mix gently and store at 4 °C for up to 7 days.

steps.title: Make MACS buffer
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 % FBS to PBS in a glass bottle, mix, then add 2 mM EDTA, resuspend and store at 4 °C for up to 7 days.

steps.title: Set up processing tubes
steps.instruction: For each sample prepare three 15 mL Falcon tubes labeled “Collection”, “Digested” and “Filtered”. Add 0.5 mL RPMI to the Collection tube and store at 4 °C (up to 72 h). Add 1 mL MACS buffer to the Digested tube and store at 4 °C (up to 72 h). Place a 0.70 µm cell‑strainer on the Filtered tube. Do not add FBS or BSA to the Collection tube.

steps.title: Pre‑heat water bath to 37 °C
steps.instruction: Set a water bath to exactly 37 °C and verify the temperature with an external thermometer.

steps.title: Prepare digestion media and incubate 20 min
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh Digestion Media (including freshly added collagenase) and add 1.5 mL to each Collection tube. Incubate tubes in the 37 °C water bath for 20 min; at 10 min gently tap and shake each tube.

steps.title: First digestion pass and collect fraction
steps.instruction: Cut a 1 mL pipette tip to widen the opening according to lymph‑node size. After the 20 min incubation, pipette the lymph node through the cut tip 5 times, then remove 1.5 mL of the digestion media (first cell fraction) and transfer it to the Digested tube kept on ice.

steps.title: Add fresh media and incubate 10 min
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL fresh Digestion Media to the same sample and incubate for an additional 10 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Second digestion pass with uncut tip
steps.instruction: Switch to an uncut 1 mL pipette tip, pipette the tissue through the tip, collect the released cells as before, add another 1.5 mL fresh Digestion Media and incubate 10 min at 37 °C. Repeat this cycle until no visible tissue remains (approximately 50 min total).

steps.title: Final digestion, centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: When the tissue is fully dissociated, transfer all remaining digested suspension to the Digested tube, then centrifuge at 350 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend, filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL MACS buffer and filter through a 70 µm cell strainer into the Filtered tube (use FACS buffer instead if flow‑cytometry is planned).

steps.title: Count cells with automated counter
steps.instruction: Dilute the filtered cells 1:10 in 0.2 % trypan blue and count using an automated cell counter (e.g., LUNA‑FX7).

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend for downstream steps
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the counted cells at 350 g for 10 min at 4 °C and resuspend at the desired concentration (see Part 3).

steps.title: Block cells with Fc‑block on ice
steps.instruction: Add Rat anti‑mouse CD16/CD32 (Fc‑Block) at 1:200 in MACS buffer (95 µL MACS + 5 µL Fc‑Block per 10⁷ cells) and incubate 15 min on ice. Prepare primary antibodies during this incubation.

steps.title: Wash cells twice
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells, centrifuge 10 min at 350 g, 4 °C; repeat once for a total of two washes.

steps.title: Stain with CD45‑biotin and CD31‑biotin
steps.instruction: Resuspend 10⁶ cells in 98 µL MACS buffer, add CD45‑biotin and CD31‑biotin antibodies diluted 1:50 (stock 150 µg/mL) and incubate 20 min on ice.

steps.title: Wash after primary staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells as described in step 16 (2 mL MACS per 10⁷ cells, centrifuge 10 min at 350 g, 4 °C; repeat twice).

steps.title: Stain with anti‑biotin magnetic beads
steps.instruction: For every 10⁷ cells add 80 µL MACS buffer and 20 µL anti‑biotin magnetic beads, incubate 15 min on ice.

steps.title: Wash after bead staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells again as in step 16.

steps.title: Resuspend for autoMACS and take pre‑sort sample
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells at 0.5 mL MACS buffer per 10⁸ cells (minimum 0.55 mL if <10⁸ cells). Transfer ~50 µL to a 1.5 mL tube for pre‑sorting purity assessment.

steps.title: Run autoMACS POSSEL program
steps.instruction: Load the suspension onto the Miltenyi autoMACS® (use the ‘POSSEL’ standard program). The run takes ~5 min per sample; positive fraction contains CD45⁺/CD31⁺ cells, negative fraction contains fibroblasts (CD45⁻/CD31⁻).

steps.title: Post‑sort centrifugation and volume adjustment
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sorted cells at 350 g for 10 min at 4 °C, then top‑up each sample with RPMI + 2 % FBS to a total volume of ~10 mL before the spin.

steps.title: Resuspend sorted cells at 10⁷ cells/mL
steps.instruction: After the spin, resuspend the cells in RPMI + 2 % FBS at a concentration of 10⁷ cells per mL.

steps.title: Count sorted cells and assess viability
steps.instruction: Count the resuspended cells with an automated counter and record viability. For higher accuracy (especially for negatively selected fibroblasts) use Acridine Orange/Propidium Iodine staining instead of trypan blue.

steps.title: Take aliquots for purity check
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL from the positively selected fraction and 30–50 µL from the negatively selected fraction into separate 1.5 mL tubes for downstream purity analysis.

steps.title: Store remaining cells on ice
steps.instruction: Keep the remaining sorted cells on ice until quality‑control and purity checks are completed.
